note: Our mapping of our framework text onto SCF identifiers. provenance=ai, confidence<1.0 — label it in the UI.

mappings.rationale: aramco_ccc.json 1.1 requires an ISO 27001-aligned ISMS; ISO 27002 has no ISMS-establishment control (that lives in ISO 27001 clauses 4-10), so only the documented policy topic 5.1 partially carries it.
aramco_ccc.json 1.2 requires defined cybersecurity roles, accountability and a designated senior management owner — exactly 5.2 roles/responsibilities plus 5.4 management responsibility.
aramco_ccc.json 1.3 mandates security policies AND procedures with at-least-annual review, matching 5.1 (policy set and periodic review) and 5.37 (documented operating procedures).
aramco_ccc.json 1.4 is a personnel awareness/training programme covering policies, threats and individual responsibilities — the literal scope of 6.3.

aramco_ccc.json 1.5 requires periodic evidence of adherence to CCC requirements on Aramco's schedule; 5.36 covers demonstrating and reporting compliance with rules and standards, though the customer-reporting cadence is contractual and outside ISO 27002.

aramco_ccc.json 2.1 is a risk assessment process (threats, vulnerabilities, impacts, treatment plans); ISO 27002:2022 contains no risk-assessment control — that requirement sits in ISO 27001 clause 6.1.2, so mapping it to any Annex A topic would be wrong.

aramco_ccc.json 2.2 is risk treatment option selection (mitigate/transfer/accept/avoid); ISO 27002 clauses are the treatment measures themselves and contain no risk-treatment-decision control — that is ISO 27001 clause 6.1.3.
aramco_ccc.json 2.3 requires managing subcontractor/fourth-party risk and flowing security requirements down the chain — 5.19 supplier relationships plus 5.21 ICT supply chain.
aramco_ccc.json 3.1 requires an accurate hardware/software/data inventory with assigned owners, which is precisely 5.9 inventory of information and associated assets.
aramco_ccc.json 3.2 requires classifying Aramco data to a scheme and applying per-level handling/storage rules — 5.12 classification, with 5.13 labelling as the marking half.

aramco_ccc.json 3.3 requires unrecoverable disposal of Aramco data when no longer needed with destruction certificates — 8.10 information deletion, and 7.14 where the carrier equipment is disposed of.
aramco_ccc.json 4.1 mandates least-privilege access policy limited to legitimate business need — 5.15 access control policy, 8.3 restriction of access to information.
aramco_ccc.json 4.2 requires strong authentication with MFA for remote and privileged access — 8.5 secure authentication, with 5.17 governing the authentication secrets themselves.
aramco_ccc.json 4.3 requires privileged accounts to be inventoried, minimised, monitored and just-in-time — the exact subject of 8.2 privileged access rights.
aramco_ccc.json 4.4 requires at-least-quarterly review of access rights with prompt revocation, which is the periodic-review requirement inside 5.18.
aramco_ccc.json 4.5 requires access removal within 24 hours of termination or role change — 5.18 covers removal/adjustment of rights, 6.5 the termination-of-employment obligations.
aramco_ccc.json 5.1 prescribes AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, i.e. the cryptographic algorithm/strength rules of 8.24.
aramco_ccc.json 5.2 covers key generation, storage, rotation and destruction — the key-management lifecycle that 8.24 explicitly includes.
aramco_ccc.json 6.1 requires perimeter protection of facilities plus authorised-only entry with access logging — 7.1 perimeters and 7.2 physical entry controls.
aramco_ccc.json 6.2 protects equipment holding Aramco data from theft and environmental threats and while in transport — 7.8 siting/protection and 7.9 assets off-premises.
aramco_ccc.json 6.3 defines secure work areas with clean-desk and screen-privacy measures — 7.6 working in secure areas and 7.7 clear desk/clear screen.
aramco_ccc.json 7.1 requires documented, tested, approved and tracked changes with rollback — the change-management control 8.32.
aramco_ccc.json 7.2 requires current anti-malware with real-time protection and scheduled scans — directly 8.7 protection against malware.
aramco_ccc.json 7.3 requires vulnerability identification by scanning and severity-based remediation — the technical vulnerability management cycle of 8.8.
aramco_ccc.json 7.4 sets a 30-day critical patch SLA; patching is the remediation step ISO 27002 places inside 8.8 rather than in a separate clause.
aramco_ccc.json 7.5 requires security event logs protected from tampering and retained 12 months plus monitoring — 8.15 logging and 8.16 monitoring activities.
aramco_ccc.json 7.6 requires firewalls and intrusion detection (8.20 networks security) and network segmentation (8.22 segregation of networks) for Aramco-connected systems.
aramco_ccc.json 7.7 requires regular, securely stored and restore-tested backups of Aramco data — the whole content of 8.13 information backup.
aramco_ccc.json 7.8 requires baseline secure configurations from industry standards with deviation monitoring — exactly 8.9 configuration management.
aramco_ccc.json 8.1 requires a documented incident response plan defining roles, procedures and communication — 5.24 incident management planning and preparation.

aramco_ccc.json 8.2 sets a 4-hour breach notification to the customer; 6.8 covers timely reporting of security events through defined channels and 5.24 the pre-agreed communication protocol, but the contractual 4-hour clock to Aramco has no ISO equivalent.
aramco_ccc.json 8.3 requires root-cause and impact/compromise investigation — the analysis steps of 5.26 incident response, with 5.28 covering the forensic evidence collected during it.

aramco_ccc.json 8.4 requires a formal post-closure report (timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions); ISO 27002 puts reporting procedures in 5.24 and the corrective-action output in 5.27, though the 72-hour customer deadline is contractual.
aramco_ccc.json 8.5 obliges giving Aramco's responders access to systems, logs and personnel during remediation — 5.26 response activities and 5.28 preservation/handover of evidence.
aramco_ccc.json 8.6 mandates post-incident review and improvements to prevent recurrence — verbatim the intent of 5.27 learning from information security incidents.
